nodes.title: Ise: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Ise. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: An enterprise is deploying Cisco ISE 3.x in a distributed architecture with two Policy Administration Nodes (PAN), two Monitoring nodes (MnT), and six Policy Service Nodes (PSN) across two data centers. Which statement about the PAN role is correct?
flashcards.back: In ISE, only the primary PAN is writeable. The secondary PAN receives replicated configuration and becomes writeable only after a failover (manual, or auto-failover if configured). PSNs handle RADIUS/authentication, not PANs, and PSNs cannot be auto-promoted to PAN. the secondary PAN is a warm standby promoted manually or via auto-failover

flashcards.front: An engineer must enforce posture compliance so that only laptops with up-to-date Windows patches and a running AV agent can access corporate resources. Non-compliant devices receive remediation resources. Which Cisco ISE feature provides this?
flashcards.back: The ISE Posture Module (inside AnyConnect/Secure Client) evaluates the endpoint against posture policies. Non-compliant devices are given a restricted dACL and URL redirect to a remediation portal (patch server, AV update). Profiling identifies devices, it does not remediate them.

flashcards.front: A Cisco ISE administrator wants non-compliant devices to be automatically quarantined and later released once remediated, without requiring manual session termination. Which RADIUS mechanism makes the switch terminate the session and re-authenticate the endpoint?
flashcards.back: RFC 5176 RADIUS CoA lets ISE push a reauthentication or session termination to the NAS in real time. ISE uses this to dynamically enforce policy changes, such as moving a posture-violating endpoint into a restricted VLAN/dACL and back when remediated.

flashcards.front: A company wants to allow contractors temporary wireless access via a self-registration portal that emails a one-time password. Which ISE feature implements this?
flashcards.back: The ISE Self-Registered Guest Portal lets visitors create an account, optionally approved by a sponsor, and delivers credentials via email/SMS. The BYOD, Posture, and MyDevices portals serve different purposes (certificate provisioning, compliance checking, device lifecycle).

pairs.stem: A Cisco ISE administrator wants non-compliant devices to be automatically quarantined and later released once remediated, without requiring manual session termination. Which RADIUS mechanism makes the switch terminate the session and re-authenticate the endpoint?
pairs.option: RADIUS Change of Authorization (CoA) with reauth or terminate action

pairs.stem: An engineer must enforce posture compliance so that only laptops with up-to-date Windows patches and a running AV agent can access corporate resources. Non-compliant devices receive remediation resources. Which Cisco ISE feature provides this?
pairs.option: Cisco ISE Posture Assessment using the AnyConnect ISE Posture Module with dACL remediation redirect

pairs.stem: A corporate policy states that privileged network device administrators must authenticate with MFA and have their commands audited. Which protocol provides command-by-command authorization and accounting?
pairs.option: Kerberos with PKINIT

pairs.stem: A corporate policy requires that laptops be automatically enrolled with a client certificate used for 802.1X EAP-TLS when joining the network for the first time. Which ISE workflow accomplishes this?
pairs.option: Guest portal with voucher code

pairs.stem: A security engineer wants an AAA design where the same policy server provides RADIUS for wireless users, 802.1X for wired users, TACACS+ for device admin, and posture checks. Which Cisco product covers all of these in one platform?
pairs.option: Cisco Secure ACS (end-of-life)

pairs.stem: A company wants to allow contractors temporary wireless access via a self-registration portal that emails a one-time password. Which ISE feature implements this?
pairs.option: Guest Services — Self-Registered Guest Portal with sponsor approval and SMS/email notification

nodes.title: Cryptography fundamentals: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Crypto is the math layer that makes the rest of security possible. Most exam questions test symmetric vs asymmetric, hashing vs encryption, when to use which, and how key management actually works in practice.

flashcards.front: Symmetric vs asymmetric encryption — when do you use each?
flashcards.back: Symmetric (AES-256, ChaCha20): one shared key, fast, used for bulk data. Asymmetric (RSA, ECC): public/private key pair, slow, used to exchange a symmetric key or to sign. Real systems use both: asymmetric to negotiate, symmetric to encrypt the bulk traffic (this is how TLS works).

flashcards.front: What's the difference between hashing and encryption?
flashcards.back: Encryption is reversible — the holder of the key can recover the plaintext. Hashing is one-way — you cannot derive the input from the output. Hashes are for integrity (did the file change?) and password storage (compare hashes, never store plaintext). SHA-256 is the modern default; MD5 and SHA-1 are broken.

flashcards.front: What is a digital signature?
flashcards.back: A signature is a hash of the message encrypted with the signer's private key. Anyone with the public key can verify (decrypt the signature, recompute the hash, check they match). This proves authenticity (the holder of the private key signed it) AND integrity (the message wasn't tampered with).

flashcards.front: Why use a key management service (KMS)?
flashcards.back: Raw key handling is hard to do safely — you have to rotate, audit, restrict, destroy. A KMS holds keys in hardware, exposes encrypt/decrypt APIs, logs every use, enforces who can use which key. Your application code never sees the actual key material. AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS all play this role.

pairs.stem: A malicious actor is performing a MAC flooding attack against an access switch, causing the CAM table to overflow so that the switch fails open and floods frames. Which mitigation stops this attack?
pairs.option: Enable port-security with a maximum number of MACs per port and a violation action of restrict or shutdown

pairs.stem: A penetration tester gains access to a VLAN through a vulnerable kiosk and sends double-tagged 802.1Q frames hoping to reach a protected VLAN. Which mitigation specifically prevents this VLAN hopping attack?
pairs.option: Assign native VLAN to the same VLAN as a data VLAN on trunks

pairs.stem: An engineer is hardening the control plane of a core Cisco IOS-XE router. Traffic destined to the router itself (routing protocol updates, SSH, SNMP) must be rate-limited and classified so that a flood of ICMP does not exhaust CPU. Which feature should be configured?
pairs.option: Storm Control on uplink interfaces with ICMP threshold

pairs.stem: An organization wants NTP to be authenticated between routers to prevent an attacker from spoofing time and forging log timestamps. Which configuration is correct?
pairs.option: Configure ntp authentication-key,.

pairs.stem: A security architect wants to prevent rogue DHCP servers on an access switch and also stop ARP spoofing between hosts in the same VLAN. Which combination of features must be enabled?
pairs.option: DHCP snooping with trusted uplinks.

pairs.stem: A security engineer wants to prevent IP address spoofing at the edge of the network so that attackers cannot forge source addresses from inside routed segments. Which IOS feature accomplishes this at the interface level?
pairs.option: Control Plane Policing

nodes.title: VPN and secure connectivity: Key Ideas
nodes.content: A VPN tunnels private traffic over the public internet, encrypting it end-to-end. Site-to-site VPNs connect networks (e.g., on-prem to cloud); client VPNs connect individual devices to a private network. Both rely on IPsec or SSL/TLS.

flashcards.front: Site-to-site VPN vs client VPN — what's the difference?
flashcards.back: Site-to-site VPN connects two networks (typical: on-prem data center ↔ cloud VPC) using gateway devices on each side. Client VPN connects an individual user's laptop to a private network for remote access. Site-to-site uses IPsec, client VPN often uses SSL or WireGuard.

flashcards.front: IPsec — IKE phase 1 vs phase 2.
flashcards.back: Phase 1 (IKE) authenticates the two peers (pre-shared key or certificate) and builds a secure management channel. Phase 2 negotiates the actual data tunnel (encryption algorithm, key lifetime). Most exam questions test that phase 1 must succeed before phase 2.

flashcards.front: When do you pick a dedicated link over a VPN?
flashcards.back: VPN over the public internet is cheap but variable — bandwidth and latency depend on internet weather. Dedicated links (Direct Connect, ExpressRoute, Cloud Interconnect) are private fiber with consistent latency and bandwidth — pick them for production traffic that must be predictable, or compliance scenarios that forbid the public internet.

flashcards.front: What's the BGP tunnel option for?
flashcards.back: VPNs can use static routes or BGP. BGP-based VPNs auto-propagate route changes between sides (add a new subnet on-prem → cloud learns it within seconds). Static VPN requires manual route updates every time the topology changes. Always pick BGP for production.

pairs.stem: A financial services company is designing an IPsec site-to-site VPN between two data centers. The security team requires Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS) so that a future compromise of the pre-shared key cannot decrypt previously captured traffic. Which IKEv2 configuration element enforces PFS on every rekey?
pairs.option: A Diffie-Hellman group specified in the IPsec (Phase 2) proposal

pairs.stem: An engineer troubleshoots an IKEv2 site-to-site VPN stuck in MM_WAIT_MSG2. Both peers have matching proposals, PSKs, and reachable IPs. Which is the most likely cause?
pairs.option: Mismatched IKEv2 lifetime values between peers

pairs.stem: An engineer deploys FlexVPN on a hub-spoke topology using IKEv2. Which feature allows spokes to dynamically build spoke-to-spoke tunnels on demand using shortcut switching?
pairs.option: IKEv1 aggressive mode with wildcard PSK

pairs.stem: An engineer configures Cisco AnyConnect (Secure Client) remote access VPN on an ASA. Which feature steers only corporate subnets through the tunnel while sending Internet-bound traffic directly?
pairs.option: Split tunneling using a split-tunnel-policy tunnelspecified ACL

pairs.stem: An engineer must decide between Cisco AnyConnect SSL VPN and IPsec IKEv2 remote access. Remote users are often behind hotel NAT and restrictive firewalls that only allow HTTP/HTTPS. Which option is most likely to succeed in all locations?
pairs.option: AnyConnect SSL VPN over TCP 443 (with DTLS fallback to UDP 443)

pairs.stem: An architect is choosing between Cisco DMVPN and GETVPN for a large multi-site MPLS backbone where all sites must freely reach each other and encryption must preserve original source/destination addresses for multicast routing. Which technology fits best?
pairs.option: Site-to-site IKEv1 mesh tunnels

pairs.stem: A healthcare company stores PHI in an AWS S3 bucket. They must ensure data is encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys and that access is restricted to specific IAM roles. Which AWS configuration meets these requirements?
pairs.option: Enable SSE-KMS with a customer-managed KMS key and restrict access with an IAM role + bucket policy referencing aws:PrincipalArn

pairs.stem: A CIO is evaluating Cisco Secure Workload (Tetration). Which primary security benefit does it provide beyond traditional perimeter firewalls?
pairs.option: Application dependency mapping and zero-trust microsegmentation enforced by host-level agents across on-prem and cloud workloads

pairs.stem: A cloud team must ensure that EC2 instances cannot reach the Internet but can call AWS services privately. Which configuration meets this?
pairs.option: Public subnet with an Elastic IP and stateful NACL

pairs.stem: Which statement about Zero Trust Architecture is accurate?
pairs.option: Zero Trust places trust primarily in the device's IP address

pairs.stem: A CASB product (Cisco Cloudlock) flags that several employees uploaded sensitive CRM records to an unsanctioned third-party SaaS. Which cloud security concept does Cloudlock address?
pairs.option: Shadow IT discovery and data-at-rest DLP in sanctioned and unsanctioned SaaS applications

pairs.stem: A container security engineer wants to ensure that only signed images from an approved registry can be deployed to a Kubernetes cluster. Which mechanism enforces this at admission time?
pairs.option: RBAC ClusterRole limiting who can use kubectl apply

pairs.stem: An engineer is configuring a Cisco Secure Firewall access control policy. A rule must inspect traffic for intrusions using a balanced Snort ruleset and also log connections. What rule action must be used?
pairs.option: Allow with an Intrusion Policy attached and Logging at Beginning/End enabled

pairs.stem: An engineer deploys Cisco Umbrella SIG for a remote branch. They want web traffic to be inspected by the cloud firewall and forwarded securely from the branch router. Which tunnel type should be configured on the ISR?
pairs.option: DMVPN Phase 3 spoke tunnel toward a hub ASA

pairs.stem: A Cisco Umbrella Investigate analyst notices a domain with a high risk score, recent registration, and fast-flux DNS. Which characteristic is the strongest indicator that this domain is likely used for malware C2?
pairs.option: The domain uses Let's Encrypt certificates

pairs.stem: A Cisco Firepower Threat Defense (FTD) deployment must block outbound connections to newly registered domains (NRDs) often associated with phishing. Which feature achieves this without maintaining a manual list?
pairs.option: Security Intelligence (SI) feeds from Talos with the Newly Registered Domains category

pairs.stem: A security team is rolling out Cisco Umbrella as the primary DNS-layer security control. The CISO requires that users on managed corporate laptops receive granular, user-level policies even when off the corporate network. Which deployment method meets this requirement?
pairs.option: Point internal DNS forwarders to the Umbrella resolvers using Cisco Secure Network conditional forwarding

pairs.stem: A developer integrates a third-party application with Cisco FMC using the REST API. The application retrieves access control rules every 30 seconds. After a week, the requests start failing with HTTP 429. What is the most likely cause?
pairs.option: The FMC is rate-limiting the client because polling frequency exceeds allowed API calls per minute
